- [FACT] Article discussed intermittent fasting (IF) and its effects on bone health.

- [FACT] The article mentioned a review published in the British Journal of Nutrition.
- [FACT] The review included studies pulled from the MEDLINE database until September 30, 2022.
- [FACT] Various IF protocols discussed in the article included the 5:2 diet, alternate day fasting (ADF), and time-restricted eating (TRE).
- [FACT] The article noted that animal studies on IF and bone health may not extrapolate to humans.
- [FACT] Observational studies suggested a link between some IF practices and compromised bone health, but lacked control for confounding factors.
- [FACT] Interventional studies indicated that time-restricted eating protocols up to six months do not adversely affect bone health and may have a protective effect.
- [FACT] ADF showed no negative effects on bone health, while no studies looked at the 5:2 diet and bone health outcomes.
- [FACT] The article concluded that more research is needed in the area of IF and bone health.
